text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Villagers in Ruiru town in the outskirts of Nairobi kill eight suspected cattle thieves and burn two vehicles.
- The National Council of Churches of Kenya expresses its reservations on a reform and anti-corruption bill published last week by the attorney-general.
- A three-year old girl is rescued 48 hours after she was kidnapped in Mombasa.
- Local Government minister Francis Lotodo urges members of the Kalenjin community to support a federal system of government to ensure they keep supremacy over land in the Rift Valley.
- A strike by air traffic controllers and staff of the meteorological department continues for a third day on Monday.
- The government and some trade unions warn workers against participating in Friday's general strike called by the National Convention Executive Council to press for constitutional reforms.
- The Church of the Province of Kenya and other religious leaders are due to meet President Daniel arap Moi this week.
- A cross-section of leaders express outrage over a call by a call by an opposition-backed alliance for a general strike.
- Opposition legislator John Njenga Mungai says the decision by the International Monetary Fund to suspend aid to Kenya is outrageous, unrealistic and unfortunate.
- Backroom wrangles in the highest ranks of government threaten to derail Kenya's economic reform program.
- Ugandan police are collaborating with military explosives experts to establish the motive and identity of grenade attackers who terrorised the capital city of Kampala last week.
- Finland joins Nordic neighbours in suspending aid to Zanzibar because of a standoff between the government of President Salmin Amour and the island's main opposition. ($1=61 Kenyan Shillings)
